extracted.intended_audience: readers and scholars of early‑modern utopian literature and designers/scholars of research institutions (readers of Francis Bacon's New Atlantis)
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive guidelines and standards for organizing an all‑encompassing research academy (Salomon’s House), covering mission, recurring external missions, experimental facilities, methods, and social/organizational practices. The text offers concrete infrastructural and procedural prescriptions as a model of institutional science.

rubrics_metrics.name: End of the foundation (mission of Salomon’s House)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The end of our foundation is the knowledge of causes, and secret motions of things; and the enlarging of the bounds of human empire, to the effecting of all things possible.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary objective is systematic investigation to uncover causes and hidden operations of nature and to extend human capacity to accomplish what is possible; institutional activities should be judged by how they contribute to these ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular exploratory missions every twelve years
rubrics_metrics.description: “every twelve years there should be set forth out of this kingdom, two ships, appointed to several voyages; that in either of these ships there should be a mission of three of the fellows or brethren of Saloman’s House, whose errand was only to give us knowledge of the affairs and state of those countries ... and withal to bring unto us books, instruments, and patterns in every kind”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic, state‑sanctioned external expeditions are mandated to gather knowledge, instruments, and patterns; ships return while resident fellows remain abroad until the next mission; ships are only laden with victuals and treasure to support fellows and purchases, not to establish commercial trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanity in laws regarding strangers
rubrics_metrics.description: “he hath preserved all points of humanity, in taking order and making provision for the relief of strangers distressed”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional and state policies towards outsiders must preserve humane relief and assistance even while restricting access; humane considerations are core constraints on other policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom to depart and inducements to remain for strangers
rubrics_metrics.description: “that of the strangers that should be permitted to land, as many at all times might depart as many as would; but as many as would stay, should have very good conditions, and means to live from the State.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission policy balances openness (freedom to leave) with incentives/support for those who choose to stay; retain voluntary residence while providing adequate provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: State control of navigation and exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: “When the King had forbidden to all his people navigation into any part that was not under his crown, he made nevertheless this ordinance ...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private or general navigation/exploration is restricted by the state to control exposure and preserve secrecy; exploration is centralized and permitted only through organized, sanctioned channels (e.g., missions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep subterranean facilities (lower region) for long‑term material processes
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have large and deep caves of several depths; the deepest are sunk 600 fathoms ... These caves we call the lower region. And we use them for all coagulations, indurations, refrigerations, and conservations of bodies. We use them likewise for the imitation of natural mines and the producing also of new artificial metals, by compositions and materials which we use and lay there for many years.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide deep, stable, controlled subterranean spaces to carry out long duration, slow, or pressure/temperature‑sensitive experiments (mineral synthesis, long fermentations, artificial metal production, conservation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burials in several earths and diverse composts/soils for material and agricultural experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have burials in several earths, where we put divers cements ... We also have great variety of composts and soils, for the making of the earth fruitful.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use varied burial media and engineered soils as experimental substrates for material transformation and for improving/creating productive soils; long‑term burial is an experimental technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: High towers and the upper region for atmospheric observation and manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have high towers, the highest about half a mile in height ... And these places we call the upper region ... We use these towers, according to their several heights and situations, for insulation, refrigeration, conservation, and for the view of divers meteors — as winds, rain, snow, hail, and some of the fiery meteors also.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build towers of varying heights to access different atmospheric strata for observation, controlled experiments (insulation/refrigeration), and meteorological study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lakes, pools, and marine sites for aquatic experiments and salinity manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have great lakes, both salt and fresh ... We have also pools, of which some do strain fresh water out of salt, and others by art do turn fresh water into salt. We have also some rocks in the midst of the sea, and some bays upon the shore for some works, wherein are required the air and vapor of the sea.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain both freshwater and saltwater bodies and specialized pools for experiments in desalination, salinization, aquatic breeding, and sea‑air related processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of streams, cataracts and engines as sources of mechanical power
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have likewise violent streams and cataracts, which serve us for many motions; and likewise engines for multiplying and enforcing of winds to set also on divers motions.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harness natural water currents and engineered engines to supply mechanical energy for experiments and operations; design infrastructure to multiply and channel wind or water power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial wells, fountains, and tincture apparatus including specialized waters
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also a number of artificial wells and fountains ... and among them we have a water, which we call water of paradise, being by that we do it made very sovereign for health and prolongation of life.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a diversity of wells and infusion apparatus to produce, age and test medicinal waters and tinctures; include specialized preparations with therapeutic claims for systematic testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled houses/chambers for reproducing meteors and airborne generation
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also great and spacious houses, where we imitate and demonstrate meteors — as snow, hail, rain, some artificial rains of bodies and not of water, thunders, lightnings; also generations of bodies in air — as frogs, flies, and divers others.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create enclosed houses capable of reproducing and studying atmospheric phenomena and generation processes under controlled conditions to observe and manipulate meteorological and spontaneous generation events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chambers of health to qualify air for curing diseases and preserving health
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also certain chambers, which we call chambers of health, where we qualify the air as we think good and proper for the cure of divers diseases and preservation of health.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sealed/controlled environments where air composition and other environmental variables are regulated for therapeutic trials and preventive health research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic baths and physiologic restoration facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also fair and large baths, of several mixtures, for the cure of diseases, and the restoring of man’s body from arefaction; and others for the confirming of it in strength of sinews, vital parts, and the very juice and substance of the body.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a range of baths and topical therapies with varied formulations aimed at restoring bodily strength and treating conditions; experiment systematically with mixtures and applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orchards and gardens for horticultural experimentation and agricultural innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also large and various orchards and gardens, wherein we do not so much respect beauty as variety of ground and soil, proper for divers trees and herbs ... we practise likewise all conclusions of grafting, and inoculating ... make them come earlier or later than their seasons, and to come up and bear more speedily ... make them greater much than their nature; and their fruit greater and sweeter, and of differing taste, smell, color, and figure ... many of them we so order as that they become of medicinal use.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experimental variety over aesthetics: implement grafting, inoculation, season manipulation, size and flavor modification, and selective cultivation to produce novel or medicinal plants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial plant generation and transmutation
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also means to make divers plants rise by mixtures of earths without seeds, and likewise to make divers new plants, differing from the vulgar, and to make one tree or plant turn into another.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental techniques include generating plants without seed using soil/mixture methods and inducing transmutation or significant alteration of plant forms; these are explicit experimental goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parks/enclosures for animal dissection, trials and physiological experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also parks, and enclosures of all sorts, of beasts and birds; which we use not only for view or rareness, but likewise for dissections and trials, that thereby may take light what may be wrought upon the body of man. Wherein we find many strange effects: as continuing life in them, though divers parts, which you account vital, be perished and taken forth; resuscitating of some that seem dead in appearance, and the like. We try also all poisons, and other medicines upon them, as well of chirurgery as physic. By art likewise we make them greater or smaller than their kind is, and contrariwise dwarf them and stay their growth; we make them more fruitful and bearing than their kind is, and contrariwise barren and not generative. Also we make them differ in color, shape, activity, many ways.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use enclosed populations for invasive physiological experiments, toxicology, surgical technique testing, breeding and size/trait manipulation, and experiments bearing directly on human medicine and physiology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedicated pools and places for fish trials and aquatic breeding
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also particular pools where we make trials upon fishes, as we have said before of beasts and birds.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain specialized aquatic environments for directed trials on fish species analogous to land animal trials; support aquaculture experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeding and generation sites for useful insects (silkworms, bees)
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also places for breed and generation of those kinds of worms and flies which are of special use; such as are with you your silkworms and bees.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide controlled rearing facilities for economically useful insects and study their generation, productivity and husbandry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental food and drink production for nutrition and medicinal effects
rubrics_metrics.description: “I will not hold you long with recounting of our brewhouses, bake–houses, and kitchens, where are made divers drinks, breads, and meats, rare and of special effects. ... We have also drinks brewed with several herbs and roots and spices; yea, with several fleshes and white meats; whereof some of the drinks are such as they are in effect meat and drink both, so that divers, especially in age, do desire to live with them with little or no meat or bread. ... some do extremely move appetites, some do nourish so as divers do live of them, without any other meat, who live very long.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with recipes, preservation, and nutritive formulations to create foods and beverages with targeted physiological or therapeutic properties; maintain specialized culinary laboratories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispensatories and pharmaceutical shops for medicine preparation and standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have dispensatories or shops of medicines; wherein ... the simples, drugs, and ingredients of medicines, must likewise be in so much the greater variety. ... for their preparations, we have not only all manner of exquisite distillations, and separations, and especially by gentle heats, and percolations through divers strainers, yea, and substances; but also exact forms of composition, whereby they incorporate almost as they were natural simples.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate pharmacies/dispensatories with extensive collections of simples and processed drugs, perform aged fermentations and refined separations, and develop reproducible composition forms approaching natural simples; emphasize technique and quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical arts, crafts, and novel materials production
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also divers mechanical arts, which you have not; and stuffs made by them, as papers, linen, silks, tissues, dainty works of feathers of wonderful lustre, excellent dyes, and many others ... and shops likewise as well for such as are not brought into vulgar use among us, as for those that are.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support artisan and manufacturing workshops for developing new materials and techniques (textiles, papers, dyes, decorative crafts) and maintain prototype/production shops for dissemination or demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse furnace and thermal regimes including imitation of celestial heats
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have also furnaces of great diversities, and that keep great diversity of heats; fierce and quick, strong and constant, soft and mild, blown, quiet, dry, moist, and the like. But above all we have heats, in imitation of the sun’s and heavenly bodies’ heats, that pass divers inequalities, and as it were orbs, progresses, and returns whereby we produce admirable effects. Besides, we have heats of dungs, and of bellies and maws of living creatures and of their bloods and bodies, and of hays and herbs laid up moist, of lime unquenched, and such like. Instruments also which generate heat only by motion.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a wide array of controlled heating technologies (variable regimes, cyclic/periodic heat patterns, biological/chemical heat sources, motion‑generated heat) to simulate environmental and celestial thermal conditions for material and biological experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational roles, employments and rites of fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: “First, I will set forth unto you the end of our foundation. Secondly, the preparations and instruments we have for our works. Thirdly, the several employments and functions whereto our fellows are assigned. And fourthly, the ordinances and rites which we observe.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional practice requires a clear specification of mission, facilities, assigned functions for fellows, and formal ordinances/rites; administration and role definition are part of institutional design and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social laws and customs promoting chastity and family propagation
rubrics_metrics.description: “They allow no polygamy. They have ordained that none do intermarry, or contract, until a month be past from their first interview. Marriage without consent of parents they do not make void, but they mulct it in the inheritors ... they have near every town a couple of pools (which they call Adam and Eve’s pools), where it is permitted to one of the friends of the man, and another of the friends of the woman, to see them severally bathe naked.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social regulations (monogamy, waiting periods before contracting marriage, penalties for non‑consensual family marriages, structured inspection practices via trusted friends) are presented as civic measures to promote chastity and stable propagation; these social norms are part of the commonwealth model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feast of the family as institutionalized social ceremony
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed ritual: when a man has thirty living descendants (all above three years old) the State funds a family feast; the father (tirsan) consults, reconciles disputes, arranges relief, chooses a son as 'Son of the Vine', receives a King’s charter and a golden cluster representing descendants, gives blessings and jewels, and presides over ceremonies and hymns praising Adam, Noah, Abraham, and thanksgiving for the Saviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ceremonial public rituals, state recognition (charter, revenue, insignia) and family governance functions (advice, reconciliation, social discipline, selection of heir/residence) are institutionalized to promote social cohesion and regulated lineage propagation.
